display.purpose: Page-level h1 only (app name, section-defining headline).

body.purpose: All running text, request/message content, form values.

label.purpose: Form field labels, sitting above the input.

shadows.name: card-ambient
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system; soft lift under cards, never a hard drop shadow.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Button hover/disabled transitions — the only motion currently in the codebase.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Below this, base font drops 18px->16px and display/title sizes step down.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Solid forest-green pill CTA — the app's one high-emphasis action style.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; border-radius: 999px; padding: 14px 28px; border: 1px solid transparent; cursor: pointer; background: #2f4a3c; color: #ffffff; transition: opacity 0.15s ease, background-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #1f3329; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2f4a3c; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 0.5; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Outline pill for lower-emphasis actions alongside a primary button.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; border-radius: 999px; padding: 14px 28px; cursor: pointer; background: transparent; color: #2f4a3c; border: 1px solid rgba(47,74,60,0.35); transition: opacity 0.15s ease, background-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: rgba(47,74,60,0.08); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2f4a3c; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Card
components.description: White bordered container on the cream page background — holds a request, a message group, or a stat tile.
components.html:
New request

Find me a flight home tonight.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e6e1d3; border-radius: 20px; padding: 24px; text-align: left; box-shadow: rgba(0,0,0,0.1) 0 10px 15px -3px, rgba(0,0,0,0.05) 0 4px 6px -2px; } .ds-card-title { font-family: Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 24px; line-height: 118%; letter-spacing: -0.24px; color: #221f19; margin: 0 0 8px; } .ds-card-body { font-family: system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 18px; line-height: 145%; color: #6b6355; margin: 0; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Pill-shaped text field with a label above it, matching the Edit Profile inspo pattern.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; text-align: left; } .ds-field-label { font-family: system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; color: #221f19; } .ds-field-input { font-family: system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; color: #221f19; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e6e1d3; border-radius: 999px; padding: 12px 20px; } .ds-field-input::placeholder { color: #6b6355; } .ds-field-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: rgba(47,74,60,0.35); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(47,74,60,0.08); }

narrative.overview:
Gavi411 reads like a trusted assistant's warm, paper-toned notebook rather than a slick SaaS dashboard: a cream page, ink-dark text, white index cards for every request and message, and a single deep forest-green accent used sparingly for action. The pairing of a serif display headline with a plain sans body signals 'a person is handling this, not a bot farm' — capable and a little literary, never cold or corporate.

This direction was extracted from the project's Design Inspo board, not invented. It is the pattern that recurred independently across three separate folders: the 'Nexus AI' screens in General layout (appearing in 5 of that folder's images), the Hebrew-language concierge chat screenshot in chat interface, and the budget-tracker screen in layout color and elemnts. The elements style folder's Serviqo AI-support kit confirmed the card/stat-tile shape and pill-input pattern specifically for a support-request product. The purple/lavender gradient screens seen elsewhere on the board were treated as anti-reference: a different product category (social/dating), inconsistent with the majority pattern.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream page background, never stark white behind the whole viewport — only cards are pure white.
One accent color only: deep forest green. No secondary or tertiary accent.
Serif display type for headlines, plain sans for everything functional.
Everything interactive (buttons, inputs) is a full pill — no rounded-rectangles for actionable elements.
Cards carry a soft ambient shadow and a hairline border, not a hard drop shadow.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Forest green is the only saturated color in the system. If a new UI need shows up wanting a second brand color, reach for a neutral or an opacity variant of green before introducing a new hue.

rules.name: The Pill-or-Card Rule
rules.body: If it's clickable/typeable, it's a pill. If it's a container, it's a large-radius card. Nothing in between.

dos: Do keep the page background cream (#f6f3ea) and reserve pure white (#ffffff) for cards and inputs only.
Do use the serif (Georgia) only for headings; body copy, labels, and buttons stay sans.
Do make every clickable/typeable element a full pill; every container a 20px-radius card.
Do keep forest green as the only accent.
donts: Don't introduce the purple/lavender gradient look seen in some inspo images — it was explicitly identified as off-brand noise.
Don't add a UI component library or CSS-in-JS dependency — plain CSS + custom properties by project convention.
Don't apply logical/bidi CSS properties system-wide — UI chrome is English/LTR only.
